recent_posts.title: Coding Challenge 188: Voice Chatbot
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step coding challenge building a voice chatbot inside a p5.js sketch using three components: speech-to-text (OpenAI Whisper via Transformers.js), a chatbot brain (ranging from simple Eliza-style pattern matching to RiveScript to a small LLM), and text-to-speech (Kokoro TTS). The tutorial covers Web Audio API for microphone capture, MediaRecorder for push-to-talk, audio buffer processing, WebGPU acceleration, and integrating HuggingFace models client-side in the browser. Multiple brain implementations are demonstrated, culminating in using SmallLM2 with a system prompt and conversation history.

recent_posts.title: Using p5.js 2.0 text features including variable fonts, contours, and 3D models
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of new text-related features in p5.js 2.0, covering how to load fonts from Google Fonts using async/await, adjust variable font weight with textWeight(), extract letter outline points with textToContours() (including sample factor and simplify threshold options), and convert text into extrudable 3D geometry with textToModel() in WebGL mode. The video also demonstrates practical use of the angle property returned per contour point to orient shapes along letter paths.

recent_posts.title: What is Transformers.js?
recent_posts.summary: Transformers.js enables running machine learning models directly in the browser using JavaScript, without requiring cloud servers or API keys. The library provides a pipeline API for tasks like sentiment analysis, language detection, and speech recognition. Integration with p5.js requires understanding ES6 modules, async/await syntax, and model configuration options including device selection (WebGPU/CPU) and data type precision (quantization). Models are loaded from Hugging Face's repository and execute locally in the browser, offering privacy and cost benefits despite some performance limitations compared to server-side solutions.

recent_posts.title: Coding Challenge 187: Bayesian Text Classification
recent_posts.summary: A live coding session implementing a Bayesian text classification algorithm from scratch using JavaScript and p5.js. The tutorial walks through Bayes' theorem fundamentals, explains naive Bayes assumptions and the bag-of-words model, demonstrates word frequency counting across categories, implements Laplacian smoothing for zero-probability handling, and builds a working classifier that categorizes text as positive, negative, or neutral sentiment. The implementation includes prior probability calculations, conditional probability chains for multiple words, and probability normalization without computing the denominator constant.

recent_posts.title: This Fall on The Coding Train
How to Load Data with p5.js (2.0)
p5.js 2.0: async and await
recent_posts.summary: p5.js 2.0 introduces async/await for loading external data, replacing the preload function and callback patterns from version 1.x. The new approach uses promises with await keywords to handle asynchronous operations like loading images, JSON, and other data. Setup functions now need the async modifier when using await, making code more sequential and readable. The tutorial covers migration strategies, common gotchas like forgetting await keywords, and demonstrates both blocking and non-blocking loading patterns.

recent_posts.title: Robot control frequencies vs human reaction times
recent_posts.summary: Explores the control loop frequencies used in physical robots compared to human reaction times. Modern humanoid robots typically require kilohertz update rates for good control, while humans can function effectively with reaction times around 100 milliseconds. Simpler robot controllers like rayboard systems can operate at much lower frequencies around 10 hertz.

recent_posts.title: Coding Challenge 186: Wave Function Collapse Overlapping Model
recent_posts.summary: The post explores the wave function collapse algorithm and its application in procedural generation. It includes a detailed explanation of extracting tiles from a source image and ensuring adjacent tiles fit together correctly. The author shares coding techniques, challenges faced, and provides a final working example for viewers interested in generative patterns in computational design.

recent_posts.title: 3D Pose Estimation with ml5.js
recent_posts.summary: The post explores 3D pose estimation using the BlazePose model in ml5.js, detailing the process of capturing key points from video using a webcam and displaying them in a virtual 3D space with the p5.js WebGL renderer. It highlights converting 2D coordinates into 3D measurements and visualizing them dynamically, along with tips for rendering and scaling.
